leftovers.park.describe.prune: Pruning parked snapshots nobody is waiting on
leftovers.park_note.usage: usage: /park-note [--token <token>] <message> — send a directive to a parked agent, delivered when it resumes (without --token: the most recently parked agent of this session)
leftovers.park_note.unknown_flag: /park-note: unknown flag %s — the only flag is --token <token>; to send a message that begins with dashes, put -- before it
leftovers.park_note.queued: noted for parked agent %s, delivered when it resumes — /resume %s to wake it now
complete.leftovers.park_note.token: send the note to this park instead of the most recent one: --token <token> <message>
leftovers.parked.prune_unknown: %d kept because nothing proves them finished (%s): they may be waiting in another process — /parked gc <age> removes by age, waiting or not
leftovers.parked.usage_prune: /parked prune — remove the snapshots proven finished (job ended, already resumed, or owner process gone); waiting parks and those of unknown state are kept
leftovers.parked.usage_gc: /parked gc <age> — remove EVERY snapshot older than <age> (e.g. 24h, 7d), including parks still waiting: their agents never resume
complete.leftovers.parked.prune: remove the snapshots proven finished; waiting and unknown ones are kept
complete.leftovers.parked.gc: remove every snapshot older than <age> (e.g. 24h, 7d), waiting parks included
leftovers.park_note.resumed: park %s already resumed — its snapshot is only kept for the record, so nobody would read the note (nothing was recorded)
leftovers.park_note.finished: park %s is finished (its scheduled wake ended) — nobody would read the note (nothing was recorded); /resume it first if you mean to continue that agent
leftovers.park_note.held_elsewhere: park %s is owned by another live process (%s) — send the note from there with /park-note; nothing was recorded here
leftovers.prompt.withdrawn: permission prompt withdrawn — the run that asked for it moved on. What you typed for it was not sent to the model:
leftovers.proc.operator_only: --all and --owner look across every session's processes: only the person at this chatcli terminal's prompt can use them (not a session, a headless surface, a scheduled job or a command issued while a turn runs). Nothing was listed or stopped.
leftovers.proc.usage_operator: At this terminal's prompt only: /proc list --all (every session's processes, with their owner) · /proc stop <id> --owner <owner> (stop one of them)
complete.leftovers.proc.all: every session's processes with their owner (this terminal's prompt only)
complete.leftovers.proc.owner: stop a process of another owner: --owner <owner> (see /proc list --all)
